sense.text:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” We are not like the others who call themselves followers and believers, who hold the Bible in their hand and it is just a book. We are the chosen people of God, and we do far more than carry the book: we read the book and we do what the book says.

The hope is real because it is written. Looking at the condition of our people, our nation, we know better days are coming, because it is written and it is promised. So we come to this Bible to find out what it is we need to be doing.

What is sin? Ask a so-called Christian and he will wiggle: missing the mark, falling short, not doing good. It is a broad answer because they don't want any responsibility. To sin means you are doing something wrong, and to know what you are doing wrong you have to go somewhere and read it. They don't want that. One sister at the 2018 Blitz said if she isn't convicted in her heart it isn't law, and God has to speak to her himself: he spoke to her about adultery but not about wearing pants. That is selective hearing. Nobody came and told her to pay that ten percent, but she does it. Don't let them run; hold them to what the scripture says.

“Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.” That is the purest definition, and it is why they hate the Israelites: we give biblical definitions, and the word of God defines itself. To transgress is to infringe, to go beyond the bounds, to break, disobey, defy, breach, violate. To sin is to break God's laws.

The first of three biblical facts: the law teaches us what sin is. “Is the law sin? God forbid. Nay, I had not known sin, but by the law.” Paul is saying he did not know what sin was except by the law.

“For I had not known lust, except the law had said, Thou shalt not covet.” He did not understand the extent of what lust was until he understood what it meant to covet. So what teaches us what sin is? The law. The Christians treat keeping the commandments of God like that is the sin, when it is the opposite.

The second fact is that sin causes us to die, and do not let the so-called Christians tell you that breaking the laws of God is okay. That is unbiblical, and it is not what Christ taught. Christ told you himself: “Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.” What Christ fulfilled was the sacrificial law, the law of sacrifice.

“Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.” Till heaven and earth departs. Read that to your Christian family and watch their faces: you will see them close their ears right in front of you. So what do you mean we don't have to keep the Sabbath day, a man can shave off his beard, a woman can wear what she wants, you don't have to keep the high holy days? Nine times out of ten they say, let me take you to the writings of Paul so you understand what that's talking about. You mean I can't just read what Christ said? I have to go somewhere else to figure out what Christ meant when he said don't think I came to destroy the law?

“Whosoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so, he shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven.” This throws a wrench in their whole belief system. Many of us were taught that no sin was greater than another, come as you are, and we said it like it was in the Bible. No: there were sins that were great, things you would do that you had to be put to death for. That is biblical.

Teaching men so means telling everybody it's all right: don't worry about that beard, don't worry about them fringes, eat what you want, live how you want. Come judgment day that one is the least, and the least gets death.

“But whosoever shall do and teach them, the same shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.” They will tell you over and over that it isn't about what you do. Christ said do and teach them. Job well done. There is no confusion there, so why is there confusion when we teach exactly what the Bible says about those who live a life full of sin?

Christ told us what happens to those who break the commandments; now Paul tells us what happens to those who break them, unrepented and not believing. “For the wages of sin is death.” A wage is a fixed, regular payment made by an employer to an employee. Sin pays, and what it pays is death.

“But the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” Eternal life is for those that do righteousness, who decide not to live in sin but to follow Christ and be like him. We are not here on buddy-buddy, because we love being around each other so much; we are here because we want to make it to the kingdom. Our actions have to say the same thing, and when we leave this building our actions still have to say we are trying to make it to the kingdom. You have to be out there just how you are in here.

precepts.why:
Where else do we read of receiving wages? “He that is unjust, let him be unjust still: and he which is filthy, let him be filthy still.” You are not changing anybody who is destined to be what they are. Our job is to find the twelve tribes of Israel that are repented: there are 144,000 men who will rise up and take this world by storm, and countless numbers of our brothers and sisters who will wake up, find out this truth and follow. “And he that is righteous, let him be righteous still: and he that is holy, let him be holy still.”

“And, behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to give every man according as his work shall be.” Christ has a reward for every one of us. Those are the wages. There are wages for sin and there are wages for righteousness. The question is which one you are working towards: where is your time going, where are you punching the clock, in righteousness or in unrighteousness? Don't think for a second you can fake it like you are on one side when you are not.

Moses spoke of the same thing. “I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing.” The blessings are in Deuteronomy 28, verses 1 to 14, us ruling the world, and the curses run from verse 15 to 68.

“Therefore choose life.” Unless you are a dummy, unless something is wrong with the way you process information, you are going to choose life. When do you question whether you want to live? When sin is before you. We all choose life or death every single day, and some of us are playing.

“See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil; In that I command thee this day to love the Lord thy God, to walk in his ways.” A so-called Christian will tell you your walk with God is on the inside, deep in your heart, not about what you do. That is not scripture; it is doctrine. People make their feelings what God feels.

Moses said “to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, that thou mayest live and multiply: and the Lord thy God shall bless thee.” Do what God said to do, and he blesses us. The Bible is not hard to understand. Christianity teaches that you get closer to Jesus by breaking the commandments, and they think they are cutting us when they say if you keep one you have to keep them all. We are going to live by all the commandments of God; if you find one we are not doing, let us know so we can change.

He called heaven and earth to record so you can't say you didn't know what to do, and today we can't say it either. It has been right in front of us. You heard the brothers in purple and gold on the corners, and you can't erase what you heard: people scoffed in front of us and then went home at night and opened their New King James and their NIVs and saw that it said just that.

sense.text: The third biblical fact: the whole Bible is law. Tell your so-called Christian grandma and your auntie and your pastors: the whole Bible is law. “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.”

precepts.why:
Ezra says the exact same thing. “This is the condition of the battle, which man that is born upon the earth shall fight; That, if he be overcome, he shall suffer as thou hast said: but if he get the victory, he shall receive the thing that I say.”

“For this is the life whereof Moses spake unto the people while he lived, saying, Choose thee life, that thou mayest live.” Ezra takes us back to what Moses said. The Bible is very redundant: everything connects and is attached to one another. Ezra equates life and death with righteousness and unrighteousness, keeping the commandments of God and not keeping them.

So do you have a choice whether or not to be in the battle, whether or not to deal with the terms and conditions set before us? No. You are here, you are breathing, you see everything in front of you, but you have a choice to make. The Bible says there are people who will see, hear, understand and still decide to follow this world. Like the white girl in the movie who hears the growling, gets up and walks right over to where the danger is: you knew death was afoot and you still went that direction. We don't know what anybody will do until the last breath is gone from them; somebody can be a complete demon and turn their life around. But this puts us in the perspective of how God really is, not a fairy-tale imagination of him. Crying and boohooing in church doesn't mean God is near you; Buddhists and Muslims cry too. You are just emotional, all up in your mind, and nothing about it is biblical.

sense.text: Back to the beginning, where it all started: how sin historically entered the world. “And the Lord God commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat.” What is that called? A commandment. If God tells you to do something, that is a commandment.

“But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.” Out of all the trees, that is the one God told Adam he could not deal with. What happens when you sin? The wages of sin is death. The Bible says the same thing over and over and over.

Notice who he is dealing with in verses 16 and 17: the man. The Lord gave the commandment to the man, and the man was to apply it and tell those under him exactly what to do. Adam was to enforce it, teach it, and make sure it happened.

“It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.” The woman wasn't there yet when that commandment was given. Brothers, this is why it all falls on you: you are the head of the house. The Lord deals with you, and you deal with your household. That is the order of things.

Did Adam enforce it? “She took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.” He did not enforce what God told him to do, and we died. She ate of it, and we all fell from there. The original sin was in the garden. Don't listen to brothers and sisters who make things up, however good the analogy and allegory spoke to your soul, however the beat hit right when the point hit. Don't fall for it.

precepts.why:
“For the devising of idols was the beginning of spiritual fornication, and the invention of them the corruption of life. For neither were they from the beginning, neither shall they be for ever. For by the vain glory of men they entered into the world, and therefore shall they come shortly to an end.”

Idol worship was the beginning. Think about it: if you do something other than what God told you to do, what god did you follow to do it? It is a god, an idol, somebody or something you put above the Lord, whether it is yourself, your own mind, or somebody telling you something. At that point you figured they had more power and you should go the direction they said. That is idol worship, and that was the beginning of it all.

“For the worshipping of idols not to be named is the beginning, the cause, and the end, of all evil.” The beginning was the worship of idols. Eve put something before God, whether herself or somebody else, and she brought it to her husband.

“Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned.” When this took place it fell on all men. Notice it still says by one man: the one being charged with the offense is the man, Adam, because he was the head and was supposed to instruct his household.

He is the head of his household, therefore he is responsible. Brothers, when your wife does something stupid, we are looking at you. When your kids are out of order, when your house is jacked up, we are looking at you. We haven't forgotten about the wife, but who is ultimately the cause? Your leadership is failing somewhere. So are you going to fix it, or whine about it: that's the woman you gave me?

“When Adam transgressed my statutes, then was decreed that now is done.” When Adam transgressed, things were made the way they are now. Above this Ezra speaks of the dangers of reaching the glorious, beautiful city and the beautiful sea: to get there you have to go through a narrow path, the only way, and a dangerous road. It became that way when Adam transgressed.

“Then were the entrances of this world made narrow, full of sorrow and travail: they are but few and evil.” The entrances are life. The path we all must walk became difficult; before, we were going to live forever and weren't worried about anything. Now we have a short life, and that short life is full of evil. Terrible things happen all through it, and if you thought that was something, wait until the next thing hits you.

“For the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit. If then they that live labour not to enter these strait and vain things, they can never receive those that are laid up for them.” If you don't go through that narrow and strait gate, you won't inherit eternal life and the heavenly mansions Christ told us are coming if we endure. You have to go through all the dangers and make it through; you won't coast. Many of us think that once we wake up to who we are it will be easy. No, that is when Satan comes for you. You didn't have these problems when you were in the world; it turns up when you come into this truth.

“For Adam was first formed, then Eve. And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression.” The woman being deceived was in the transgression; we read that strong. But who took it? The fact is she messed up, but it is your house.

“Of the woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die.” Why is that written? Things written aforetime were written for our learning. Adam messed up, we saw how he messed up, and so we have to keep the woman, our wife, in check. Do not think for a second she is not trying to overthrow you. Even with a Proverbs 31 woman you will be maintaining that order until you die; call it marital maintenance, continually establishing your role in the household.

It is the same with brothers and with kids: any establishment of order has to be maintained, because people will generally try to run over you if you allow them, and kids will push the envelope to see how far they can get. Structure and order must be maintained at all times. But don't misread it either: sometimes she just wants to know what you want to eat tonight.

Ezra gets to the root of things. “O thou Adam, what hast thou done? for though it was thou that sinned, thou art not fallen alone, but we all that come of thee.”

“It had been better not to have given the earth unto Adam.” Why does Ezra say this? He is looking at the end result of what happened. Little by little the scriptures show what went down in the garden: Adam was given dominion over everything. “Or else, when it was given him, to have restrained him from sinning.” This is Ezra in his man mind trying to come up with a solution to the problem of man: you could have made Adam so that he could not sin.

“For what profit is it for men now in this present time to live in heaviness, and after death to look for punishment?” Heaviness in this life, and then die and look for punishment. “For what profit is it unto us, if there be promised us an immortal time, whereas we have done the works that bring death?” He is doing the same thing Paul did, showing the fight between the flesh and the spirit, because in this life all men are messing up. Ezra doesn't even realize he is asking for a savior, and we needed one, because there was no coming back from there.

“And that the glory of the most High is kept to defend them which have led a wary life, whereas we have walked in the most wicked ways of all?” Ezra was righteous, but he was real about himself, and he equates himself with those who fall short. Many of us act like we can't believe it when someone messes up, when we all fall short. We all live the same life, battle the same flesh and deal with the same thoughts; Ezra just recognized it.

sense.text:
Sin begins with deception. “Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made.” Subtil is the old spelling of subtle: delicate, faint, difficult to detect. He came to her, and it was difficult for her to realize he was trying to deceive her and trick her. Its second sense is making use of clever and indirect methods to achieve something. Do you think anything has changed? Some of us say the devil isn't going to get me, I've been doing this too long. The scripture says he is subtil for a reason.

“Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?” That was the first deceit. She could have answered, yes, he said we can eat of any tree. The first thing he tries to do is deceive you in your own thoughts: maybe you forgot, maybe you didn't remember.

“We may eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden: But of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, God hath said, Ye shall not eat of it.” She caught herself. So the first thing he did was try to confuse her.

“Ye shall not surely die.” Now he is casting doubt: die, what's that? You're not going to die. “For God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened.” Sure, you will understand more: you will understand how you are going to die, now that you are going to die as God said. That is the fullness of the understanding he gave her.

He caused confusion, he caused her to doubt, and then he lied to her, and she took and ate. Do we not see that today? All of those things she was supposed to combat, and where was the fight supposed to happen? In her mind. The forefront of the battle takes place in your head, or your heart however you want to see it. We forget that we have all the tools we need right here, and if it doesn't sound right, it isn't right.

precepts.why:
“But I fear, lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ.” Subtilty is deceit, deception. Where was she deceived? In her mind. Where is the battle fought? In your mind. That is where he plays on your thoughts, and it is happening right now.

So the question is, what have you filled your head with, what have you equipped yourself with? Not memorizing scriptures: if you think that is being equipped, something is wrong with you. You are supposed to read and understand the Bible and see it as truth; once you believe, you have what you need to fight against sin. Without understanding, without proper fear towards God, you are going to get out here and get your ass whooped, thinking you are in the fight. People in the church swinging their hats around, dancing and stomping on the floor think they are fighting the devil, and they are getting their behinds whooped and don't even realize it.

We cannot allow our minds to be corrupted and tainted by this world, by the thoughts of Satan and the things he tries to instruct us to do. Nobody here is ignorant of being tempted and persuaded to do something they know is wrong.

sense.text:
“In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not.” Pay attention: the god of this world. Remember the original sin was idolatry. Where is he fighting them? In their minds. This is where everything takes place. If your mind is weak, meaning your spirit is weak, you will not be able to fight. That is why the Bishop has told us for years: study, pray and apply. Without application you are just reading a book; you might as well pick up Harry Potter or Lord of the Rings. If you don't see that these things were written aforetime for your learning, what are we doing?

“Lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them.” That is the whole intent of Satan: to blind the mind so they cannot see the truth. How many of us fought the truth when we first heard it? Pulling out John 3:16 with a New King James with no dust on it, thinking we knew something, and getting our whole face fixed. That is what Satan wants: for you to think you know something, to think you are loved by the Lord because you were washed in the blood and got baptized. So you're saved, you're good? No, you're not.

precepts.why:
Notice it said the god of this world. Has anybody seen Satan? There is a realm where all this fighting takes place, and they have literal access to you in this realm. You can't see it with your eye, but you know it is there.

“Wherein in time past ye walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air.” In times past, when you were in the world living like everybody else, you walked according to the prince of the power of the air, and that is Satan, the devil. In this earth, this realm, this world, you are following one of two. That's it. If it isn't the Most High, it is a derivative of Satan. However it is divided up, whatever confusion you fall under, if it isn't of the Most High it is one of Satan's devices: worshipping the woman, holy pomegranates, cows. Any type of delusion out there, Satan has many.

“The spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience.” The spirit working with those who disobey God is the spirit of the prince of the power of the air. These religions get mad when you tell them they follow the devil: Islam, Jesus, witchcraft, however you want to mark it up, you are following a delusion.

That air is his airwaves too: social media, TikTok, the media you see. Satan controls and runs that algorithm, which is why you are scrolling and all of a sudden, boop, you wonder how that got there. It is the prince of the power of the air.

“Hereafter I will not talk much with you: for the prince of this world cometh.” Christ is warning the apostles about his departure, and he says when he leaves Satan is coming. You don't see him, but Christ said he is coming, and that lets you know his presence is really here among us, just as the spirit is really among you if you believe and keep the commandments and faith. That should scare the mess out of you. Some people are used to it and say it's not a big deal. The hell it isn't.

“We know that whosoever is born of God sinneth not; but he that is begotten of God keepeth himself.” To be born of God means you believe, you walk after the commandments, and you believe on his son. “And that wicked one toucheth him not.” The way you keep yourself is by keeping the commandments; when you do that you are protected, because the wicked one can't touch you. You have on the full armor of God and he has no access.

“And we know that we are of God, and the whole world lieth in wickedness.” Those out in the world follow the prince of the power of the air, all of them. If they don't follow the Most High, they are following Satan. That isn't the first thing you can explain to somebody, because in their mind they believe in Jesus. But Christ himself told you: you say Lord, Lord, and don't do what he says. Just saying Jesus won't get you in the door; you have to follow. Those out there in the world are under a certain control, just as those that are of the Lord are under a certain control.

sense.text: We understand how sin works: that realm is trying to tap into yours, trying to break into your temple. “Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God: for God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man.”

“But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” The things you are tempted by are your own inner lust, your own inner thoughts. You are not going to be tempted by two homosexuals kissing, and you are not going to be tempted by bacon once you have seen the videos of the worms coming out of it. You will be tempted by something you want, something you are attracted to. The things that entice you are the things that are in you. If it is enticing you, it is there, and you would be a fool to ignore that you are being tempted and that the spirit is there.

If you keep scrolling and your phone keeps pulling up twerking, Satan keeps sending you those videos to get you to sin. It is little things, little nudges. Don't think it came out of nowhere and boom, you're in the midst of sin; that isn't how it works, and that wouldn't be deceptive. It is little nudges here and there that cause your mind to wander, because the battle takes place in your mind. He throws an NBA highlight here and a joke there, then drops it right in, you pause a split second too long, and he has seen you.

There is a whole other realm that can see what you can't, and they see your weaknesses. You don't get to pick your weaknesses when you are born. Some brothers get stricken with that weird stuff, and maturity lets you know that is a demon he was born with, a weakness he has to fight. Remember: full of sorrow and travail, and very painful.

“When the unclean spirit is gone out of a man, he walketh through dry places, seeking rest, and findeth none.” There are spirits that leave a man's body when he repents, and they scour the earth looking for somebody else to devour.

When they can't find another body to go into, they try to come back to the same person. “I will return into my house from whence I came out; and when he is come, he findeth it empty, swept, and garnished.” Empty, swept and garnished means Christ has left.

“Then goeth he, and taketh with himself seven other spirits more wicked than himself, and they enter in and dwell there: and the last state of that man is worse than the first.” Seven more demons have cleaved to him, which is why that person bugs out so far. This is not an allegory. Christ is not lying; he is telling you what these spirits are like. We can't see them, but they are there, and not just a couple: they are everywhere, looking for a host, for somebody with the weakness, who did not armor themselves, whose mind isn't built for this, somebody they can jump in and destroy.

How many brothers have we seen come in here, and now their mind is gone, their spirit is gone, Christ has left the building, and they are into all types of stuff. Kids too. And it isn't only lust: envy, malice, hatred, jealousy, all these spirits are looking for someone to jump on, and if you are not girded up you will fall.

When you and your wife are at each other's throats, there is a demon in there between you with his hands on your shoulders, his hand over your ears and eyes, so you don't hear or understand anything. Afterwards, when you finally gain control over your members, you realize how stupid it was to argue over the last bit of milk in the fridge or the last drumstick. Ask yourself why. It is them. There has to be at least one spiritual person in the room who can see it when it starts to rise. When you see things going left, drop to the ground, grab your wife, and tell her Satan is in here, he is trying to get us, and you are not going to let it happen. Watch what that does. Just don't body slam nobody.

“Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour.” This is a biblical fact: we know Satan is lurking, so we are going to be sober and vigilant, watching, head on a swivel like on security, because the moment you look away is when he tries to get you. Imagine somebody outside your house who has told you, I'm trying to break in, and when you slip I'll be up in there. What are you going to do? The Lord told us Satan is looking and waiting to get in, and we have to make sure he doesn't. We have to keep ourselves girded.

That is why we tell brothers and sisters to come around and be around each other. Christ said where two or three are gathered he is there, so where two or three are gathered it is very difficult, not impossible, for Satan to be there too.

None of us is going to fight a full-grown 550-pound male lion by ourselves. We all lose that battle alone against a roaring lion.

“Whom resist stedfast in the faith, knowing that the same afflictions are accomplished in your brethren that are in the world.” Everybody is going through it, the same afflictions. We have to be mindful.

The path to sin is not always obvious. You can be heading that way and not even know it, thinking you are walking uprightly while you take no counsel and do things on your own. “There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death.”

How do you keep from falling victim to that? Don't trust your own mind: get counsel. You would be surprised how many things you could avoid by seeking proper counsel. But know who you take counsel from; counsel from somebody not fit for counsel is stupid counsel, like telling you to whoop her with the belt because the rod driveth away sin. You're going to jail.

Seek counsel before your ventures and enterprises, no matter how long you have been in this. Everybody needs another opinion and a different perspective, and you surround yourself with men who see things differently because you don't always have all the answers. That is what sin will do: have you thinking you are going the right direction when you are not. People like that often can't be won back because they think they know everything, and pride comes before the fall. It is okay not to know sometimes and to find out from somebody. We are all men.

Be careful that you aren't the one who can't be told anything. “Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God.” Does an evil heart of unbelief come in one day? No, it is a process. You can sit here a long, long time, at all the high holy days smiling in everybody's face, and be hardened as we speak.
“But exhort one another daily, while it is called To day; lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin.” The hardening comes through the deceitfulness of sin.

precepts.why:
Another form of hardening. “He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck.” You can't tell that person anything; his mind is made up. He has been corrected so many times he has become numb to it, and it is nothing to him.

Being stood up in front of the congregation is supposed to be so demeaning, so embarrassing and shameful that you never want to be there again, and you do whatever you can not to bring shame to your household, your name and this gospel. Some folks have been stood up so many times that it is nothing: let me get this over with, do my time, and I'll be back. That is scary. Are you reprobate? Why are you still here if you aren't going to apply anything?

“Shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.” That means one of two things: put out of the body never to return, or death. Either way you die. That's a scary thing, when you can't take correction and it rolls right off your shoulder.

“Thou hast stricken them, but they have not grieved.” Being stricken by God isn't pleasant, and they didn't even grieve. “Thou hast consumed them, but they have refused to receive correction: they have made their faces harder than a rock.” We are that hard-headed: we want to be right so bad, and live the way we want so bad, that we will go against God.

This is where it all boils down. When the scripture gets read, you find out what you are dealing with. Brothers, when your wife is acting like a damn demon, read her the scripture and see what you've got; sisters, the same with your husband. If the person doesn't concede when the scripture is read and they know they are in error, you know what you have. The word of God is supposed to strike fear in you; it is no longer your wife or your husband talking, these are God's words. Tell your wife you hate her and she gives you the scripture, what man ever hated his own flesh, and if anything comes out of your mouth other than I had the devil on me, you are the damn devil. You don't have him on you, you are him.

“Therefore I said, Surely these are poor; they are foolish: for they know not the way of the Lord, nor the judgment of their God.” Poor here isn't money; it is poor in spirit and in understanding. They don't even understand what is coming, acting a fool for a hundred years on earth and giving up an eternity of everlasting life in the kingdom to be in pain for eternity, because they chose the prince of the air over the Most High God.

“I will get me unto the great men, and will speak unto them; for they have known the way of the Lord.” The great men are the ones who have the understanding. “But these have altogether broken the yoke, and burst the bonds. Wherefore a lion out of the forest shall slay them.” Christianity tries to take away the fact that God is mad at us because we won't do what he says, and tells us just believe in Jesus and we'll be good. They don't know the Bible: “because their transgressions are many, and their backslidings are increased.”

Still the man who has hardened his neck and his heart. “There is an exquisite subtilty, and the same is unjust; and there is one that turneth aside to make judgment appear.” These are the ones who pretend to take correction while they know deep down they have no intention of changing. They hang their head and act so sorry, and before the crow they are right back at the nonsense, going back to their vomit. It is a show, because they fear the eyes of men and don't fear God. We have to watch for these spirits around us.

sense.text: Why do people think they can keep doing these things? “Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.” Imagine every time somebody committed adultery they blew up, both of them, boom, gone. There would be no adultery. You would answer, are you stupid, you know we're both going to blow up as soon as this happens? Know that there is a poof and a bam coming. Because the sentence has been prolonged and pushed back, we think we have time.

precepts.why:
There's no time. “Say not, I have sinned, and what harm hath happened unto me? for the Lord is longsuffering, he will in no wise let thee go. Concerning propitiation, be not without fear to add sin unto sin: And say not, His mercy is great; he will be pacified for the multitude of my sins.”

That is the last thing you should be saying: the Lord will be cool, he isn't worried about that, the Lord knows my heart, I don't normally do things like this. We point to the men in the Bible who messed up, King David, King Solomon. You aren't David, and you aren't Solomon, and you might not be here much longer if you keep thinking like that, acting like you'll be around forever and will never get caught. When the husband comes home and catches them, nobody feels bad for either of them; both consented, and whatever happens after the fact, even the law understands it.

sense.text:
Knowing this, you must guard yourself. “And no marvel; for Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light.” For Satan to be transformed into an angel of light he has to have the ability to do so. Is there anything he can't be transformed into? No. Some think it only means white is Jesus. It could be your bishop, your deacon, your officer, your captain, your husband, your wife, your child. What are you going to allow to deceive you?

We are all here because of the word of God; if you are here for anything else you are bugging. We didn't come together as a clan of friends who happen to be black and happen to be Israelites; we are here because we know what the Bible says. That relationship is contractual, strictly the law of God, and if you go outside of it you will be forgotten like anybody else until you repent.

“Therefore it is no great thing if his ministers also be transformed as the ministers of righteousness; whose end shall be according to their works.” Be not deceived: he is out here, lurking, trying to destroy you, appealing to your lust, your pride, your desire and the cares of this world.

“For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.” None of it is of the Lord. This world we live in is temporary; we are on proving ground. Don't get comfortable here; this is not the land of rest. Everything here is perishable and is going to burn, so don't put stock in any of it.

If your aspirations don't line up with being a prophet or prophetess of God, if you aren't aligning your life to do the will of the Lord, teach his people and bring the Israelites back to who they are, you are on the wrong path. We sit up planning to be slaves: we have been in captivity so long we don't know anything else, and our people don't even know we are in captivity. Not that you can't be a doctor, but that isn't who you are. We are prophets first, and we do whatever we can to support our people and contribute to this work.

“And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever.” Don't chase the cares of this world and the lust of the flesh, whatever inclinations you have. Chase after the laws of God. Don't let your flesh overpower you and have you out here sinning and destroying your name.

precepts.why: “Go not after thy lusts, but refrain thyself from thine appetites.” Read beside 1 John 2:16, the lust of the flesh and the lust of the eyes are the things we are not to go after. We have to make sure we are not chasing the cares of this world and the lust of the flesh, but refraining ourselves and chasing after the laws of God.

sense.text:
The prince of this world causes you to gradually normalize sin. Nobody just jumps into it; it is the perfect storm. A married brother and his wife have been at each other's throats forever, and then the one at work is soft-spoken, calls you sir, asks if she can get you something, does everything you wish your wife would do. Now the storm is perfect, and you are out here a fool. Gotcha.

Christ warned us: “And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold.” We are living in that time. Iniquity has abounded and the love of many has waxed cold. People don't know what's what. Iniquity has abounded so much that it is now wrong to keep God's commandments.

precepts.why:
“Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter! Woe unto them that are wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight!” This is the world we live in now, where they call good evil and evil good.

The Bishop put a question to the class: how would we truly feel if within the next minute Esau were no longer ruling us, every Edomite gone, and we were in charge right now? We would be in trouble. It would be complete pandemonium, because we just read it: woe unto them that call evil good and good evil. All the righteousness we think will spread to the four corners of the earth, our own people would call wrong and want to take us out. Imagine coming out of here like Israel out of Egypt and going into the wilderness with the bonnets and hair hats, the twerking, the gangs and the fraternities. Impossible. We are not there yet, but we are going to get there.

This is the present world we live in. “The wicked walk on every side, when the vilest men are exalted.” The vilest men are the ones who run the world, and that is why everything evil is called good and everything good evil. It isn't only religion; it is every aspect of life. Everything has been turned upside down, and that is why God has to raise us up to flip the world right side up again.

That is why what we say sounds so strange and unfounded to the world: they don't know God, they have been following the prince of this world, and the prince of this world has blinded their eyes. Christ said that in a little while the world would see him no more, but we would see him. We are here to take those shutters off.

sense.text:
“Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves.” This takes actually doing it, all of us: taking a step back and looking at ourselves. When somebody passes away, when the Day of Atonement comes, it reminds us to look at ourselves and see where we are slacking, because we want to make our calling and election sure. We are supposed to do it daily. If you are one of them, you have to be moving like one of them; you don't turn it off. You are who you are supposed to be at all times, and that takes constant self-examination, because the adversary the devil is lurking. You could have the devil on you, or be living with the devil right now, and think you are right.

“Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates?” To be reprobate is to be void of understanding, void of the laws of God, void of shamefulness, void of fear. That is a scary place.

“If they sin against thee, (for there is no man that sinneth not,) and thou be angry with them, and deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them away captives unto the land of the enemy, far or near.” It absolutely happened. We sinned against God, he delivered us to the other nations, and we were carried far away from our borders, where we are unto this day in our captivity.

“Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives”: if we remember who we are, right here in Babylon the great. “And repent.” Repent is not a cliche word, not the repentance you heard in church. True repentance is turning away from sin and keeping the commandments of God. It means you have to change: stop doing what you were doing wrong and now do what is right. The definition has morphed. Now they tell us to repent of racial idolatry, which wasn't heard five years ago. How many times is the word Israelite in the Bible? How am I worshipping my race by acknowledging who I am?

“We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness.” This is us confessing our faults before the Lord. The only way to do that is to examine yourself and be real with yourself. Don't hide the sin; then you are just faking it. The Lord knows what you are doing. The question is whether you will forsake it and truly change.

“And so return unto thee with all their heart, and with all their soul”: sincerely and truthfully. “Then hear thou their prayer and their supplication in heaven thy dwelling place, and maintain their cause.”

“We have transgressed and have rebelled: thou hast not pardoned.” Confessing our faults is part of making supplication. We have not been pardoned. We are yet this day in our captivity; we haven't been delivered yet. Your friends run around saying I'm delivered, but we haven't been saved yet. We have to endure until the end to be saved.
“Thou hast covered with anger, and persecuted us: thou hast slain, thou hast not pitied.” This shows the Lord isn't playing.

“Thou hast covered thyself with a cloud, that our prayer should not pass through.” We rebelled and transgressed, the Lord sent us into captivity, and he covered himself with a cloud so our prayers would not pass through. He put that cloud there because he does not hear sinners.

“Thou hast made us as the offscouring and refuse in the midst of the people. All our enemies have opened their mouths against us.” All the other nations have opened their mouths against us. “Fear and a snare is come upon us, desolation and destruction.” This is the current state of Israel right now, because of our lack of obedience. God put that cloud there, he has not pardoned, and we have to go through it.
“They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and cast a stone upon me.” That is the jails.

“I called upon thy name, O Lord, out of the low dungeon. Thou hast heard my voice: hide not thine ear at my breathing, at my cry.” This is why we keep the commandments of God, so he will hear our prayers. But it won't happen until we acknowledge our offense, acknowledge what we have done, and repent.

precepts.why: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.” He withdraws until we acknowledge our offense; it fits the cloud that our prayer should not pass through.

“He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be abomination.” This fits too: turn away from the law and even the prayer is abomination, so it does not pass through. Write these precepts down.

This is the one. “Now we know that God heareth not sinners.” That is the Bible, and that is why he put the cloud there: he doesn't hear sinners. We rebelled and we transgressed; he has not pardoned, and we are still here in captivity.

sense.text: “And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together.” It is speaking of coming together, congregating. Any time you are able to come together, you should be trying to come together. Some of us let Satan mess with us through an introverted approach to life, and we only see you here. You don't have to be bubbly and around everybody all the time, but there should be somebody you have a relationship with and see during the week, some function, a mission, a fundraiser, something. When you forsake the assembling, your spirit weakens. Those who separate themselves weaken themselves.

“Therefore let us not sleep, as do others.” Don't let us sleep. We have to be up, woke, observant, because Satan is out here. He doesn't care about your status. He is trying to take out those who are doing what God said and who are going to be infectious; he attacks the ones who can make the biggest impact. If you wonder why you are getting jacked up, you are a threat. The one not going through anything isn't doing anything, and Satan isn't worried about him. But those who could be influential in raising brothers up, teaching and guiding, Satan is coming for you.

“For they that sleep sleep in the night; and they that be drunken are drunken in the night. But let us, who are of the day, be sober.” Of the day means of the light. “Putting on the breastplate of faith and love; and for an helmet, the hope of salvation.” We have to be armored up, because that is what it takes to fight. Without it you will lose. However much you lift and however fast you are, it means nothing: if you aren't spiritually strong, you are weak.
